701836.t: From ἄρχω (árkhō, “to begin, to be first in order”) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

701860.t: Of disputed origin: * From Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥-sḱe-ti (“to start, rule”), which appears to be an inchoative formation from *h₂er- (“to fit, put together”), thus “to begin to fit together” > “to start, rule”.

701837.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “beginning”) + ἡγέομαι (hēgéomai, “to lead”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

701818.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(w)ə́rsēn, from Proto-Indo-European *wérsēn (“male”); however, dialectal attestations show it had no initial digamma in Greek, and it has been argued that the initial w was lost in the Greek, Armenian, and some Indo-Iranian forms of…

701820.t: From αἴρω (aírō, “to raise; to lift; to elevate”) + -σις (-sĭs).

701862.t: A noun use of the present participle of ἄρχω (árkhō, “to rule”).

701829.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *ártos, of unknown further origin, though likely borrowed from a substrate. Compare Basque arto (“maize”), Old Spanish artal (a type of empanada).

701826.t: Appears to be a locative of a derivative of the root Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to fit”). Compare ἀραρίσκω (ararískō), Old Armenian արդ (ard), Lithuanian arti, and Latin ars.

701814.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + ῥώννυμι (rhṓnnumi, “to strengthen”) + -τος (-tos).

701823.t: The word is of Iranian origin (see Old North Iranian *ṛdba-, Old Persian *ṛdva-) and ultimately from Akkadian 𒅈𒁕𒁉 (/⁠ardabu⁠/, “capacity measure of about 56 litres”), found as Aramaic 𐡀𐡓𐡃𐡁 (ʾrdb) / אַרְדְּבָא (ʾardəḇā) / ܐܪܕܒܐ (ʾardəḇā), (Classical Syriac…

701806.t: A loanword from Biblical Hebrew עירבון / עֵרָבוֹן (ʿērāḇōn, “guarantee, deposit”), or from a common third source, probably Semitic.

701809.t: From ἀ- (a-) + ῥήγνυμι (rhḗgnūmi, “to break, shatter”) + -τος (-tos, adjective suffix).

701856.t: From ἀρχιτέκτων (arkhitéktōn, “architect, master craftsman”) + -ία (-ía), from ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “master”) + τέκτων (téktōn, “craftsman, builder”).

701839.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “a beginning, origin”) + -θεν (-then, “a suffix added to nouns to form adverbs of place from which: from”)

701805.t: From the same uncertain origin as ἁρπάζω (harpázō).
